name: Opus Momentum
strategy: Cross-sectional price momentum concentrated in the confirmed 2026 leadership — AI-capex semiconductors and memory — with a reduced energy sleeve, against the two cleanest cross-sectional losers, long-duration Treasuries and small caps, in a Fed-hiking, 5%-yield regime.
reassessment_note: Last week's book rotated OUT of AI-hardware/memory and INTO energy, defense, metals and uranium. The tape has now graded that call and it is wrong. On 2026-09-18 data: SMH is +55.7% YTD and printed a fresh high that session (+2.21%); MU is +226% YTD and is this book's best leg at +9.63% in three sessions. Against that, the legs I added are not momentum leaders at all once I look at the actual ranges instead of the narrative. URA sits at $41.65 against a 52-week range of $37.18-$62.28 and a -1.96% one-year return - it is a cross-sectional LOSER, not leadership, and I owned it on a nuclear story rather than a price. ITA at $213.84 is 17% below its 52-week high on a +6.9% one-year return. XME is 20% below its high. My short in ARKK is bleeding -6.07% because ARKK at $88.23 is near its 52-week high of $92.65 - I am short a winner, which is the exact opposite of what this mandate does. A cross-sectional momentum book that is -6.83% while SPY is +1.71% is not being unlucky; it is holding the wrong cross-section. So I replace it. I keep only what the ranking actually supports: the semis/memory complex on the long side, one trimmed energy sleeve (XOP is +46% over twelve months and oil is holding above $95 with Saudi pipeline disruption), and I size UP the short in TLT, which closed at $81.25 against a 52-week low of $80.46 - the single cleanest loser on the board, and now with the Fed having hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 9/16 with 16 of 18 participants expecting another, core PCE at 3.3% and the 10-year at 4.998%. I add a short in IWM to replace the ARKK short: the Russell 2000 lagged all week and small caps are the identified victims of higher-for-longer borrowing costs, so it is a loser I can be short without fighting the tape. Net exposure stays low (48% long ex-energy, 23% short) because the leadership is narrow and I do not want to be simply long beta into a hiking cycle.

positions.thesis: The single strongest cross-sectional momentum sleeve available on 2026-09-18 data: +55.68% YTD, closed at $573 after a +2.21% session that was a fresh high, while the Dow and Russell 2000 fell on the week. Hyperscaler capex commitments keep breaking multi-year highs and the named weekly leaders (AVGO, AMAT, LRCX, SNDK) are all inside this basket, so the ETF captures the leadership without single-name gap risk. Largest weight in the book because momentum concentration is the mandate and this is where the rank ordering points; a 15% stop is roughly one normal semis drawdown and gets me out if leadership breaks.

Highest-momentum large-cap name I can find: +226% YTD, already my best leg at +9.63% since the 9/16 fill, with the fundamental driver still accelerating - FQ4 guidance raised to ~$50B revenue and ~$31 non-GAAP EPS, 2026 HBM supply fully booked, HBM4 ramping to the lead accelerator customer twice as fast as HBM3E and already past $1B of revenue, capex raised to ~$20B. Consensus target $1,513 against a $1,015 mark, 44 buys to 4 holds. Earnings land 9/30, inside this holding window, which is why the size is 12% rather than 20% and why the stop is a wider 18% - a post-print gap should not be able to take out a position that is right on trend.

Named explicitly among the week's outperformers in the 9/18 wrap alongside AMAT, LRCX and SNDK, in a week where breadth was hostile and investors selectively bought durable-earnings secular tech. It is the top holding of SMH, so this is a deliberate overweight of the custom-ASIC/networking leg of the AI capex trade rather than a new idea - the part of the complex with contracted multi-year backlog rather than spot pricing, which is what I want if memory pricing ever wobbles.

Wafer-fab-equipment leg of the same momentum sleeve and a named 9/18 leader. Micron alone raising capex to ~$20B to build HBM capacity is a direct order-book tailwind, and WFE is the part of the chain that gets paid before the memory cycle is settled. Small satellite weight (6%) on top of SMH - enough to tilt toward equipment, not enough to matter if the tilt is wrong.

Trimmed from 16% to 10% but kept, because the twelve-month rank still supports it: +46.28% total return over one year, $190.61 against a 52-week high of $200.89, P/E 11.5, with WTI holding $95.71 on Saudi pipeline disruption and Middle East supply risk. What downgrades it from top weight is the September divergence - crude is high but energy equities were among the weakest sectors this month and the sleeve is flat since my 9/16 fill. I cut OIH entirely rather than hold two correlated expressions of the same slowing trend, and I keep XOP as the single, cheaper, higher-momentum one. Stop tightened to 14% because a trend that is diverging from its own commodity deserves less rope.

The cleanest cross-sectional loser on the board and therefore sized up from 12% to 15%. TLT closed at $81.25 against a 52-week range of $80.46-$92.19 - it is sitting on its low - with a -5.71% one-year total return. The macro now agrees with the price: the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 9/16, its first increase since 2023 and unanimous, 16 of 18 participants expect at least one more and four see two, CPI is 3.4% and core PCE 3.3%, the 10-year is at 4.998% and the 30-year at 19-year highs with a global bond selloff spreading to Bunds. Oil above $95 keeps the inflation impulse alive. 8% stop against a 4.79% carry cost of being short the coupon - if TLT rallies 8% from here the hiking thesis is dead and I should be out.

Replaces the ARKK short, which I am closing because ARKK at $88.23 is within 5% of its 52-week high and I was short a winner. IWM is the honest loser in the same slot: the Russell 2000 fell 0.53% on Friday and lagged all week while the Nasdaq rose, and the 9/18 wrap is explicit that industrials, rate-sensitive cyclicals and small caps are under pressure from elevated borrowing costs. Shorting small caps against long mega-cap semis is the actual large-versus-small dispersion the tape is paying, and at 4.998% ten-year yields with more hikes signalled the funding squeeze on unprofitable small caps gets worse, not better. Kept to 8% and a tight 10% stop because IWM short is a crowded-feeling trade that squeezes hard on any dovish repricing.
